title: LLM-INSTRUCT at UZH Shared Task 2026: Constraint-Aware Retrieval and Selective Debate for Paragraph-Level Argument Mining
abstract: Winning system for the UZH Shared Task 2026 on paragraph-level argument mining in UN and UNESCO resolutions. Using open-weight models limited to 8B parameters, the approach combines constraint-aware retrieval with a selective multi-agent debate to identify argumentative paragraphs and predict argumentative relations.

title: FaLCon: Facet-Anchored Retrieval with Late Consensus for Sim2Real Text-Based Person Anomaly Search
abstract: Text-based person anomaly search involves retrieving real-world pedestrian images from detailed natural-language descriptions using models trained primarily on synthetic data. This Sim2Real setting is challenging because visually similar candidates may differ only in subtle actions, object interactions, or appearance attributes, while applying multimodal LLMs to the entire gallery is computationally expensive. We propose an anchor-constrained coarse-to-fine retrieval framework that combines global semantic matching with fine-grained verification: full and concatenated captions act as anchors to preserve recall, while appearance, action, and object facets provide bounded corrective evidence, integrated through robust per-query calibration and soft claim-aware fusion. The candidate pool is refined by a Qwen3 reranker and two semantic verifiers (anomaly-aware cloze completion and multi-agent evidence reasoning), with an uncertainty-gated consensus that reweights the experts on ambiguous queries. On the PAB benchmark the full framework reaches 95.41% mAP@10, 94.44% R@1, and 99.09% R@5.

title: GeoRoute: Geometry-Aware Hybrid Inference for Traffic Future-Frame Prediction
abstract: Long-horizon future-frame prediction matters for autonomous driving, traffic surveillance, and intelligent transportation, yet suffers from temporal ghosting, geometry drift, and inconsistent object motion. Latent video diffusion models produce impressive visuals but destabilize structured traffic scenes over long horizons. We present a training-free inference framework that stabilizes reliable static structure in pretrained video predictions through multi-frame temporal context and view-conditioned routing. For front-camera videos, a multi-frame depth-layered renderer projects static geometry from observed history frames while preserving dynamic regions from the generative base model; for heterogeneous views, a frozen vision-language model infers a coarse camera group and selects a specialized motion predictor. Requiring neither retraining nor fine-tuning, the framework is validated on the AI City Challenge Track 5 benchmark, achieving competitive performance among the top-ranked teams.
